001.text: Choose one canonical engine repository and document how the original, 2.0, and Android repositories relate.

002.text: Identify the exact tested commit that each distributed desktop build and Android APK runs.

003.text: Reconcile open Android pull requests and branch differences before claiming a feature is released.

004.text: Merge or close reviewed experimental branches; prevent multiple conflicting installation paths.

005.text: Replace contradictory “ready for release” claims with current, version-specific evidence.

006.text: Maintain a capability matrix: implemented, unit-tested, live-tested, device-tested, unsupported.

007.text: Create a clean-checkout installation test with no hidden locally installed dependencies.

008.text: Standardize installation, model setup, server launch, mobile pairing, and shutdown.

009.text: Add a tested migration path from older memory, settings, and user data versions.

010.text: Separate demo/placeholder features from real functionality in every interface.

011.text: Bench-test real answers for accuracy, usefulness, consistency, reasoning, code, and casual dialogue.

012.text: Stop showing desktop fallback text as if a real model generated it; identify the failed provider.

013.text: Require an inference smoke test before a provider is marked truly working, not just an installed key or model.

014.text: Modernize obsolete or unavailable default cloud model identifiers and validate current API compatibility.

015.text: Make model routing depend on task capability, latency, cost, and past success rather than a static list alone.

016.text: Preserve user-selected provider and model; never silently substitute a paid cloud provider.

017.text: Add formal model capabilities (vision, tools, structured output, context length, streaming).

018.text: Implement structured tool-calling schemas and validate arguments/results.

019.text: Distinguish facts, assumptions, estimates, speculation, and genuine unknowns in the answer.

020.text: Evaluate whether response-plan and self-critique heuristics actually improve output quality.

021.text: Provide stable multi-turn conversation handling, including clarifications, contradictions, and corrections.

022.text: Add model/timeouts/retry behavior with useful errors, not accidental generic responses.

023.text: Track per-model token counts, throughput, cost and latency in reproducible benchmarks.

024.text: Rewrite verdict logic: two medium/high-rated sources with no detected contradiction must NOT automatically prove a claim TRUE.

025.text: Remove hard-coded confidence values unless measured and calibrated against a labeled test set.

026.text: Judge whether evidence actually supports/refutes the specific user claim, not just whether trusted sites were retrieved.

027.text: Avoid using .gov/.edu/domain reputation as a substitute for claim-level evidence quality.

028.text: Map every factual claim to the exact cited passage, source URL, and retrieval timestamp.

029.text: Show why a source supports, contradicts, or does not address a claim.

030.text: Handle misinformation repeated across many websites as one underlying unsupported claim, not independent confirmation.

031.text: Distinguish source absence from evidence of falsehood; correct the likelihood labels accordingly.

032.text: Account for stale pages, publication dates, changed facts, and retrieval failures.

033.text: Avoid claiming web/search coverage is exhaustive when engines, pages or scrapes fail.

034.text: Improve contradiction extraction beyond keyword matching; compare the same proposition and timeframe.

035.text: Harden scraper text extraction, retries, rate limits, canonical URLs, and duplicate handling.

036.text: Evaluate search relevance and citation faithfulness on a fixed research benchmark.

037.text: Treat prompt-injection checks as one defense layer, not proof that retrieved text is harmless.

038.text: Separate scientific feasibility assessments from moral or arbitrary “impossible” keyword labels.

039.text: Unify or clearly separate desktop chat history, Android SQLite sessions, user facts, long-term project memory and research knowledge.

040.text: Replace default hash-vector embeddings with a tested semantic embedding backend; keep hash only as an explicit degraded fallback.

041.text: Add hybrid semantic and keyword retrieval with metadata filters and source-based ranking.

042.text: Replace process-dependent Python hash() memory IDs with stable UUID or content identifiers.

043.text: Make JSON memory and profile writes atomic and safe under concurrent desktop/mobile access.

044.text: Add versioned schemas and migration tests for saved memories and knowledge indexes.

045.text: Use provenance, creation time, last verification and confidence for each stored fact.

046.text: Distinguish user instructions and preferences from unverified content and automatically inferred details.

047.text: Implement memory corrections, deduplication, conflict detection, expiry and deletion propagation.

048.text: Offer meaningful project-specific memory for repository state, objectives, bugs, tests and decisions.

049.text: Improve long-conversation summarization; the current simple clipping can discard crucial context.

050.text: Re-evaluate context budgeting; default maximum context is 12,000 characters, not a model-aware token budget.

051.text: Allow larger formats and better extraction (PDF/DOCX/code/images) beyond current text/markdown/JSON/CSV ingestion.

052.text: Provide export, encrypted backup, restore and selective wipe of every stored memory family.

053.text: Create a true task/planning/execution agent instead of only markdown agent descriptions and intent routing.

054.text: Add a repository checkout/worktree manager and safe isolated task branches.

055.text: Provide read/search file tools with permissions and bounded output.

056.text: Provide controlled write/patch tools with diff previews and easy restoration.

057.text: Provide shell and test execution in an isolated, resource-limited environment.

058.text: Use reproducible environment setup, package installation policy and dependency caches.

059.text: Reproduce reported failures before attempting code edits.

060.text: Implement a detect → plan → patch → test → inspect → retry loop with stopping conditions.

061.text: Require evidence of successful tests and feature checks before reporting a repair as complete.

062.text: Open GitHub pull requests with descriptions, test results, diffs and rollback instructions.

063.text: Track individual tasks and dependencies, including owner, status, blockers and acceptance tests.

064.text: Let the agent resume a stopped session from persisted state without replaying risky writes.

065.text: Add safe GitHub, CI, issue, and release integration with narrow authorization.

066.text: Let the agent escalate repeated failure, missing permissions or unclear requirements instead of looping indefinitely.

067.text: Apply explicit budgets for code-edit attempts, API spending and compute time.

068.text: Support independently reviewing an AI-generated patch before merging.

069.text: Turn “self-improvement” into measured, versioned changes; do not let the agent rewrite itself without evaluations.

070.text: Create a capability registry for tools, apps and linked accounts, with per-tool schemas.

071.text: Separate read-only operations from state-changing operations and require appropriate approvals.

072.text: Enable file management, web navigation, browser automation and computer-use as independent adapters.

073.text: Build scheduling, reminders, recurring tasks and change monitoring with durable background workers.

074.text: Add idempotency keys and recovery logs for any action that could be repeated after a crash.

075.text: Add meaningful task progress, cancellation, retry and timeout semantics.

076.text: Provide tool outcome verification from observable state, not assistant-generated success text.

077.text: Restrict network and filesystem access separately for research and software execution.

078.text: Keep user-visible action history: inputs, approvals, results and artifacts.

079.text: Build plugin/connector auth with renewable tokens and revocable permissions.

080.text: Implement capacity limits and prioritization for simultaneous workflows.

081.text: Complete physical Android-device tests for chat, file ingestion, gallery, research, image generation, saved sessions and lifecycle changes.

082.text: Finish desktop/mobile parity for advanced router tuning, detailed diagnostics, streaming and workflow controls.

083.text: Provide true token-by-token mobile streaming; the current adapter accumulates streamed chunks before returning.

084.text: Fix desktop/mobile shared JSON writes with a single transactional store or cross-process locking.

085.text: Complete and test secure remote HTTPS/VPN connectivity from home and cellular networks.

086.text: Handle computer sleep, network switching, backend crashes and reconnect without duplicate actions.

087.text: Add server job progress, cancellation, queue position, expiry and clear recovery messages.

088.text: Review the single-worker server bottleneck and separate GPU inference from fast metadata operations.

089.text: Revisit 16,000-character request and ~1 MB file limits if serious document/code analysis is required.

090.text: Make clear that the native APK depends on a running computer/server; offline phone inference is not implemented.

091.text: Implement an optional truly on-device offline mode only if that is a product requirement.

092.text: Test accessibility, keyboard/rotation, backgrounding, notifications and Android versions.

093.text: Validate real ComfyUI and Automatic1111 workflows from the phone end to end.

094.text: Merge or deliberately reject the open “Live / Files” GitHub Pages PR; test its new APK and static site separately.

095.text: Warn and verify that GitHub Pages “live-bank” files are public and do not change native app code or run models.

096.text: Measure first-token latency, total latency, tokens/sec, RAM, VRAM, CPU and GPU across target models.

097.text: Test model quality on the intended hardware and offer sensible quantized model presets.

098.text: Avoid loading large local models at the same time as memory-intensive image pipelines when resources are tight.

099.text: Apply adaptive context sizes based on the model’s actual token window.

100.text: Cache embeddings, document parse results and safe research requests with invalidation rules.

101.text: Reduce duplicate provider/status/network calls triggered by Streamlit reruns.

102.text: Separate fast replies from deep research and code-agent jobs so short questions stay responsive.

103.text: Add streaming and intermediate status for long research and generation jobs.

104.text: Profile large core, planner, and Streamlit UI modules before refactoring.

105.text: Set bounded concurrency, queue sizes, memory limits and cancellation policies for heavy jobs.

106.text: Track performance regressions automatically, including before/after hardware and model metadata.

107.text: Audit direct arbitrary-URL fetching in the original web_research_module for SSRF and access to private hosts if reachable through an API.

108.text: Recheck DNS-to-connection validation and redirects in the mobile URL ingester to guard against rebinding and unsafe egress.

109.text: Limit tool execution to sandboxed, permissioned directories, commands and network destinations.

110.text: Keep secrets out of repo files, image metadata, model prompts, logs and mobile APKs.

111.text: Add token rotation, rate limiting, revocation and stronger per-device access controls for remote deployment.

112.text: Encrypt or otherwise appropriately protect sensitive memory and stored chats, including backups.

113.text: Avoid accidental public upload of data through GitHub Pages live-bank, Git commits, logs or demo modes.

114.text: Define a single-owner access model and audit permissions before considering multi-user accounts.

115.text: Test prompt injection through webpages, documents, tools, and code comments with a hostile-content benchmark.

116.text: Use atomic writes, migrations, checksums, snapshots and tested restoration for research/memory databases.

117.text: Use dependency vulnerability scanning and signed/trusted download processes.

118.text: Create a consent and approval flow for risky operations and show exactly what changed.

119.text: Ensure model/provider failover cannot accidentally transmit local private documents to a remote API.

120.text: Extract Streamlit UI tab renderers from the roughly 105 KB app.py, in testable units.

121.text: Decompose the roughly 79 KB NexusCore module into smaller orchestration services.

122.text: Add a dedicated Python CI workflow; the main Python branch has no .github/workflows entry.

123.text: Run the full suite in CI with the correct tests/ discovery path, not root unittest discover alone.

124.text: Add type checking, formatting, linting and security scanning in CI.

125.text: Pin/lock dependency versions to reproduce releases and document compatible Python versions.

126.text: Build integration tests that exercise real Ollama and optional cloud providers rather than mocked responses alone.

127.text: Make citation accuracy, hallucination resistance, model fallback and research verdict quality release gates.

128.text: Test Android backend + native UI + phone + real model as a complete system.

129.text: Require green CI for pull requests and track release builds to specific Git commit SHAs.

130.text: Write a current architectural decision record, code owners, issues/milestones and definition of done.

131.text: Replace outdated reports that claim only 2 tests pass or state 2026-05 working-tree issues as current facts.

132.text: Implement logging/metrics that separate actual errors, model failures, tool failures and degraded-mode fallbacks.

133.text: Set up backups, crash recovery, graceful startup/shutdown and recovery from failed updates.

134.text: Create signed desktop and mobile builds with automated clean-machine installation and upgrade testing.

135.text: Publish versioned releases, change logs, known limitations, and rollback procedures.

136.text: Decide whether the default product is an everyday assistant, research workbench, software agent, or a selectable set of modes.

137.text: Simplify the 11-tab desktop UI into task-oriented views with an advanced diagnostics switch.

138.text: Show model, provider, data locality, cost, response time and whether tools really ran.

139.text: Show source-to-claim references and conflicting evidence in a browsable research report.

140.text: Provide a project dashboard for active bugs, build state, agent progress, time estimates and recent GitHub changes.

141.text: Offer model performance recommendations tailored to available hardware.

142.text: Support a correction/feedback workflow that gets tested rather than merely saved.

143.text: Create first-run guided onboarding, import/export and a one-click diagnostics bundle with secrets redacted.

144.text: Improve mobile and desktop accessibility, discoverability and error recovery.

145.text: If desired: add microphone/voice, image understanding, OCR, screen understanding and video input as separately tested capabilities.

146.text: If desired: add multi-agent delegation, benchmarks against commercial assistants and collaborative shared workspaces.
